description: Hypergravity Testing of Thawing Rates in Frozen Sand is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Michael Gardner, University of California Davis (ucdavis.edu). The active layer above permafrost experiencing seasonal freeze-thaw can range from a few centimeters to tens of meters in thickness, which complicates physical modeling of this phenomenon. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Permafrost, Cryosphere, Frozen Ground, Active Layer, Centrifuge. Published 2025-06-11. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
